leads.author: Vasilis Dragon
leads.claim: Take A = dbbi minus M91 letter by letter (a=0..z=25, mod 26), where M91 = 'incaseyoumanagetocrackthistheprivatekeysbelongtohalfandbetterhalfandtheyalsoneedfundstolive' (sha256 2fbfbef7...). A = VOZIJBDTIQBRGVEOMZNBC|YOUWON|XCPKW... with YOUWON at index 21; he splits 21/49/21 into a 7x7 frame. 'Borrow rail' (1 where dbbi_i<M91_i): its only run of 7+ ones starts at 21. 'VIC rail' (M91 letters not in the top row FUBCDORA): its longest run (9) also starts at 21. faed self-keyed Bifid -> BTCSEED..., rail2 first row 'tsedomk' reversed = KMODEST; K at (2,5) in a dbbi[:13] Bifid square -> 'BE' => 'YOU WON - BE MODEST'. Hashes: sha256(dbbi)=71fe4625..., sha256(A)=f1785730..., sha256(YOUWONBEMODEST)=e8f32510...
leads.reaction_rebuttal: Rafael Gomes (#66749): the reproducible core reaches TSEDOMK; KMODEST->BE is interpretive. The author admits step 4 is 'a reach' read backwards from the expected answer, and that the {1,4,21}/21-row split is not reproducible and came out statistically null in his own tests.
leads.our_spotcheck: Steps 1-2 reproduce exactly: YOUWON at index 21, sha256(A)=f17857308a886531..., and the only borrow run of 7+ ones is at 21. However, the borrow rail is NOT independent of A. dbbi uses only the letters a-i, so with no borrow A_i is at most 'I'. Any A letter from J to Z therefore forces a borrow, and YOUWONX forces 1111111. The VIC rail also depends only on M91's letters. The only real signal is one 6-letter English word in a single difference string, and many texts and operations have been tried, so this is most likely a coincidence. BTCSEED was already rated a coincidence in cycle 37.

leads.author: حسین ▪️ (claim); Sebastian (rebuttal)
leads.claim: In the Part4 Bifid output (btcseed...), drop the first 6 chars and take every other char (rest[::2]). That channel uses only {b,c,d,e}. Map d=00,c=01,b=10,e=11, then take 132 symbols from offset 27 = 264 bits = a checksum-valid 24-word BIP39 phrase 'dust trophy mule tragic corn ... copy satoshi fee allow' (entropy 445d1e45...ed520).
leads.reaction_rebuttal: Sebastian checked all 24 mappings x 151 offsets (3624 windows). 13 windows give checksum-valid phrases, against about 14 expected by chance. Offset and length are free parameters. Nothing matches under BIP44/49/84 or as a raw key. The prize address is a vanity address and cannot come from BIP39. Sparky: 'LLM crap'. The {b,c,d,e} channel itself is real and is a known structural property (the 2-bit selector stream of the value/selector pairs).

leads.author: MrNobody
leads.claim: Read dbbi as a straddling checkerboard with row prefixes {b,g}. It parses into exactly 64 tokens using exactly 16 distinct symbols, matching a 64-character hex digest. He claims faed has no valid hex reading at any prefix count. He brute-forced all 16! (2.09e13) symbol-to-hex mappings in two passes (41.8T trials, 13 GPU-hours, the second pass with no assumption about the plaintext): zero hits. He did not say which blob/KDF was the test target. He also notes that a random sha256 hex digest pushed through a 9-column checkerboard passes all ten of the usual 'noise' tests, so 'dbbi/faed are noise' only rules out readable language.
leads.reaction_rebuttal: No rebuttal in this chunk.
leads.our_spotcheck: The parse reproduces: 64 tokens, 16 distinct symbols, ending cleanly. {a,b,g} also gives 64/16, so {b,g} is not strictly unique. In a shuffled-dbbi control (same letter counts, any 1-3 prefix set) only 0.8% of shuffles give 64/16. This is the strongest new structural lead in this chunk. His negative brute force cannot be audited because the target and success test were not stated.

leads.our_spotcheck: The salt e2991cdcd2c957f9 does not match our phase32-inner (b45a5e3d...), salphaseion-small (3ab58534...) or cosmic (2d3f6fe0...) blobs. Phase 3 and phase 3.2 salts were not checked. Worth a single deterministic decrypt if the blob can be identified.

leads.author: Loupi; 👑; Whore Amazing; Denis Golovkin
